citation: J. P. Gordon, "Theory of the soliton self-frequency shift", Opt. Lett. 11, 662-664 (1986)
note: Neither the paper nor its abstract could be read (publisher page behind a bot check; the abstract is elided in Crossref and Semantic Scholar). The hard reference is the first-order perturbation (moment) result for a sech^2 soliton with each Raman model's own response function, derived in run.py and README.md; it is Gordon's integral over the Raman gain in form. The T0^-4 law in its long-pulse limit, -8 |beta2| T_R / (15 T0^4), is the textbook form (G. P. Agrawal, Nonlinear Fiber Optics, section on the Raman-induced frequency shift).

referenceNumbers.where: long-pulse limit of the perturbation integral (analytic); described as 'roughly the inverse fourth power of the pulse width' for the paper in secondary sources
perturbation integral with the model's h(t), computed in run.py

referenceNumbers.value: a 250 fs soliton at 1.5 um in a fibre with D = 15 ps/(nm km) shifts by its own spectral width in about 100 m
referenceNumbers.where: abstract, as paraphrased by a search result (not read); 250 fs is taken as the intensity FWHM, the spectral width as the sech^2 FWHM 0.315 / 250 fs
two secondary sources with unknown units and normalisation

ramanModels.silica: Blow & Wood, IEEE JQE 25, 2665 (1989): damped oscillator tau1 = 12.2 fs, tau2 = 32 fs, fR = 0.18
ramanModels.linAgrawal: Lin & Agrawal, Opt. Lett. 31, 3086 (2006): damped oscillator + boson peak (tau_b = 96 fs), fR = 0.245
ramanModels.hollenbeck: Hollenbeck & Cantrell, JOSA B 19, 2886 (2002): 13 modes, intermediate broadening, fR = 0.18

assumptions: N = 1 sech^2 soliton at 1550 nm, beta2 only (D = 15 ps/(nm km), beta2 = -19.13 ps^2/km), gamma = 1.3 /(W km), no self-steepening, no loss.
The shift is followed to Omega T0 ~ 0.05 (four segments with probes; the slope of a line through the five centroids).
The auto-sized grid of the engine is used (its time step is 3-25 fs, coarser than the 12 fs Raman oscillation for T0 >= 100 fs).
